items.name: Lo contour
items.tip: Low contour: a gentle low shelf for weight and warmth in the bottom end.

items.name: Bass harmonics
items.tip: Bass harmonics: adds overtones to the bass so it stays audible on small speakers.

items.name: Process
items.tip: Process: the sonic-maximizer effect. Delays the lows and mids a tiny bit behind the highs and lifts the highs when the mids are quiet, for clarity and punch.

items.name: Air
items.tip: Air: a smooth high shelf at 9 kHz (up to +4.5 dB) for sheen, plus an exciter that adds new harmonics above 5 kHz for brilliance and excitement. The exciter runs 2x oversampled, so it stays smooth.

items.name: Air exciter
items.tip: The shaper that makes the Air harmonics. The stack version gets gritty and fuzzy when Air is pushed high.

items.name: Squeeze
items.tip: Squeeze: how much each of the three bands is evened out, pressing loud parts down and lifting quiet ones up. More = denser.

items.name: Push
items.tip: Push: raises the level going into the squeeze and the limiter for more loudness.

items.name: Opto
items.tip: Opto: extra LA-2A style leveller on top of whatever the squeeze style already uses. Slow, smooth, program-dependent compression that thickens leads and bass. 0 = only what the style brings.

items.name: Squeeze mode
items.tip: Squeeze style: each style is a different chain. Gentle keeps dynamics natural. OTT presses the loud down and lifts the quiet up hard. Dance Master is a controlled multiband compressor with soft knee, auto release and a limiter on each band. Glue is mild and sticky. Slow Smooth is slow and smooth, like an opto. Punchy lets the attack through. Tight Lock clamps hard and fast. Lift brings up quiet parts. Hardstyle Lock is fast and firm with extra low-end control. Highs Tamer holds back harsh highs on leads (good after a reverb). Thick Supersaw is a slow, soft squeeze that pairs with the Opto knob to fatten supersaw leads.

items.name: Loudness match
items.tip: Loudness match: a slow level follower lifts the processed sound back up to the level that went in, so heavy squeeze or opto settings never lose volume or loudness. Auto switches it on as the Opto amount grows. It only ever lifts, and never past the Ceiling.

items.name: Warm
items.tip: Warm: saturation on the whole signal. Rounds peaks and adds body. With a Warm character other than tanh it adds disto, transistor or fuzz grit when pushed.

items.name: Clip
items.tip: Light peak clipper: pushes the signal up to 9 dB harder into a smooth clipper at the Ceiling, then the limiter. Shaves the peaks so the whole thing can sit much louder.

items.name: Ceiling
items.tip: Ceiling: the output limiter never lets the signal go above this level.

items.name: Warm character
items.tip: What the Warm knob does. Shipped is the plain tanh. The others are the PurrOne colour stages, oversampled 2x. Stack grows from drive to transistor to fuzz as you push Warm.

items.name: Clipper position
items.tip: Where the Clip stage sits. Post (before the limiter) keeps the squeeze natural and is what mastering clippers do. Pre clips the input before everything.

items.name: Mix
items.tip: Mix: dry/wet blend for parallel processing.

items.name: Output
items.tip: Output: final level. Match it with the bypassed level when comparing.

top.name: Preset menu
top.tip: Factory presets (our own). Use the arrows to step through them.

top.name: Randomize
top.tip: Set the controls to random values (output level and on/off switches are kept).

top.name: Nasty range
top.tip: Nasty range: lets Drive, Fuzz, Squeeze, Warm and the other heavy knobs go far past 100 % for really nasty, OTT and Vengeance style sounds. Off keeps every knob at its normal top.

top.name: Limiter
top.tip: Safety limiter on the output: keeps the level from ever passing 0 dBFS, smooth and transparent. Turn it off if you want the raw output (for example to let your own limiter do the work).

top.name: Settings
top.tip: Settings: version, link to the GitHub page for new versions

top.name: Info bubbles (i)
top.tip: Info bubbles: hover a control for one second to see what it does. Click to turn them off or on.
